# Compacted Summary: Chapter 1 (Complete and Final – Updated 29)

## Setting and Time
- **Season/Period**: Spring through late August, then Christmas/New Year period of the first year; now nearly three weeks into the new year (1832)
- **Primary Location**: Middlemarch and surrounding areas (Lowick, the Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Wilhaven, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Salmere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton)
- **Atmospheric Details**: Baker's boy frequently late; wind off water with salt and tar smell; dog barking periodically; bees in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreling over fish heads; carts with turnips; frost silvering hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw; children chasing hoops down lane; bell for vespers ringing thinly; chalk sun on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; light going early at end of August; starlit darkness; frosty air in late year
- **Secondary Characters/Background**: Ilrine Corrett, herbalist; Eldette Corrett, cooper; Thidrek Corrett, smith; Ridan Corrett, glazier; Jotho Corrett; Aessa Hollwood, ferryman; Cotho Hollwood, mason; Halan Hollwood, shepherd; Ulvie Hollwood, weaver; Thiena Hollwood, glazier; Elnar Brackwood, weaver; Senelle Brackwood, ferryman; Jovus Brackwood, miller; Madan Brackwood, scribe; Cotho Brackwood, shepherd; Tassa Brackwood, weaver; Colan Lindson, born at Quenwick; Islis Lindson, shepherd, born at Quenwick; Movie Lindson, weaver; Mrs. Abel, housekeeper at Stone Court; Mr. Abel

## Main Characters

**Dorothea**
- Recently widowed; residing at Lowick Manor
- Strong admiration for Caleb Garth's work knowledge; hopes to improve land and build good cottages
- Final Grange encounter: Will declared best is over, would live like one who saw heaven in trance
- Mistakenly believed Will's words referred to Mrs. Lydgate; experienced certainty his conduct with Rosamond should be above suspicion
- Though thought she might be what Will cared for most, doubt overcame this; credited all to friendship and obstruction from Casaubon's codicil
- Saw Will with portfolio on road; felt pang leaving him behind; wished they could have been happy thinking of each other
- Forced to keep money under Casaubon's codicil that ought to have been Will's, causing distress
- **Bulstrode's Report**: Described as "a woman of most munificent disposition" in possession of funds she can well spare; has destined chief part of funds to another purpose; willing to consider taking Bulstrode's place in relation to Hospital; wishes ample time to mature thoughts; setting out on journey into Yorkshire with Sir James and Lady Chettam; her decision regarding Hospital contribution will depend on conclusions about land she is to see there

**Will Ladislaw**
- Spoke impetuously at Grange about what forbidden him by own pride and honor
- Passionate love for Dorothea which he forbade himself to utter; what kept him silent was that she was forced to keep money that ought to have been his
- After parting: certainty had much more bitterness; had no assurance she loved him
- Still at Middlemarch despite weeks since parting; frequenting Lydgate's household; warbling continually with Rosamond (scandal spreading per Mrs. Cadwallader)
- Raffles knows connection between Will and Bulstrode but deliberately conceals this as card to play
- Father was at Boulogne very ill; mother's family engaged in "respectable thieving line"; mother (Sarah) ran away after Archie Duncan rejected her
- Rejected Bulstrode's money; stated unblemished honor and unstained birth important; recognized stain through mother; refuses "ill-gotten money"; departed with determined quickness
- Wrote brief letter to Dorothea asking permission to call at Lowick

**Caleb Garth**
- Met Bulstrode regarding stable drainage at Stone Court
- Working with railroads: measured and valued outlying piece of land at Yoddrell's farm belonging to Lowick Manor; confronted laborers preparing to interfere with railroad agents
- Decided to take Fred Vincy on as assistant with desk-work and accounts; offered eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Character: ruled absolutely only on other people's behalf; on ninety-nine points Mrs. Garth decided, but on hundredth point Caleb was immovable ruler
- **Stone Court Opportunity**: Consulted by Bulstrode on farm management; advised against mere bailiff, recommended yearly letting of land, stock, and implements with proportionate share of proceeds; alluring idea occurred to Caleb—what if Fred Vincy could be placed at Stone Court under Caleb's management responsibility? Would be excellent schooling for Fred; Fred could make modest income while gaining business knowledge; elated prospect of children being married by-and-by
- **Vision and Current Plans**: Pleased Fred's mind had run on Stone Court for years before Featherstone died; would be pretty turn of things for Fred to hold place in good industrious way after taking to business; Bulstrode might let him gradually buy stock
- **Critical Moral Moment with Raffles**: Took up Raffles in his gig after Raffles got down from coach and was walking beyond turning from toll-house; Raffles had recognized Caleb from previous meeting at Stone Court with Bulstrode; Caleb saw Raffles was ill and provided shelter; felt right thing to carry him under shelter
- **Final Confrontation with Bulstrode—Moral Firmness**: When Bulstrode sent note to Lydgate at Hospital and prepared to ride to Stone Court, Caleb made firm declaration: must request Bulstrode put business into other hands; obliged to Bulstrode for handsome way of meeting him about Stone Court letting and other business but must give it up; spoke with firmness that was very gentle; when Bulstrode attempted to dismiss Raffles as disreputable fellow spreading slander, Caleb stated: obliged to believe Raffles has told him truth; can't be happy working with Bulstrode or profiting by him; hurts his mind; must beg Bulstrode to seek another agent
- **Merciful Resolution**: When Bulstrode tried further appeals, Caleb waved him off with merciful intention to spare pitiable man; said what Raffles told him will never pass from his lips unless something unknown forces it from him; acknowledged if Bulstrode led harmful life for gain and kept others out of their rights by deceit, he must repent—must want to go back but can't; that must be bitter thing; not for Caleb to make Bulstrode's life harder; stated he doesn't judge as wicked or righteous, doesn't know everything; a man may do wrong and his will may rise clear out of it, though he can't get his life clear; that's bad punishment; if it is so with Bulstrode, Caleb is very sorry for him but has feeling inside that he can't go on working with him; stated as to speaking, he holds it a crime to expose a man's sin unless clear it must be done to save the innocent; promised good-day

**Mary Garth**
- Staying at Lowick Rectory with Miss Farebrother and Mrs. Farebrother
- Told Farebrother: "I have too strong a feeling for Fred to give him up for any one else"
- Upon Fred telling her of engagement with her father, touched keenly; scolded him for not seeing Farebrother's delicate feeling
- Earnestly desired to be clear she loved Fred best; determined to watch over her affections and constancy
- Currently telling stories to children at Lowick Parsonage (Rumpelstiltskin tale); Fred seated near her, watching with admiration

**Fred Vincy**
- Age four-and-twenty; son of Mr. Vincy; rejected Church vocation; took degree
- Encountered Caleb Garth at Yoddrell's farm; accepted eighty pounds for first year, more after
- Mr. Vincy responded with profound surprise and cutting disappointment; will keep no horse for Fred
- Casually mentioned to Rosamond what he heard about Casaubon's codicil mentioning Ladislaw
- Acknowledged debt to Caleb which will never be discharged
- At Lowick Parsonage: seated near Mary during storytelling; watching her with admiration
- Billiard room incident: encountered Lydgate gambling; felt shock; old opinion of Lydgate as prig reversed
- **Farebrother's Intervention and Warning**: Farebrother drew Fred aside at St. Botolph's; confessed temptation to let Fred go wrong; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound" and liable to change; claimed another man might win "firm place in her love as well as respect" through "companionship of ready sympathy" even over longest associations; Fred seized by uncomfortable chill; tone changed to encouraging; Farebrother spoke of returning to old intention and uttering warning; moment produced regenerating effect in Fred

**Mr. Lydgate**
- Doctor/physician; age nine-and-twenty
- **Financial Crisis Deepening**: Debt amounts to three hundred and eighty pounds at Brassing; creditor Mr. Dover holds bill of sale on furniture; Dover's agent has now put a man in Lydgate's house
- **Gambling Incident and Aftermath**: Played at billiard-table; won repeatedly but ended by losing four to five pounds overall; felt unmixed disgust next day; carried unpleasant vision
- **Contemplating Leaving Middlemarch**: Began familiarizing imagination with step unlike his remembered self—considering whether to quit Middlemarch; questioned whether purchaser of practice forthcoming; against step was obstacle that Rosamond in poor lodging would not find life to save her from gloom
- **Bulstrode's Medical Consultation and Opportunity**: Note from Bulstrode requested Lydgate call at Bank; Bulstrode had hypochondriacal tendency; Bulstrode announced plans to cease personal share in Hospital management due to anticipated withdrawal from Middlemarch
- **Direct Appeal for Financial Help**: Made direct statement to Bulstrode of his financial position; revealed he slipped into money difficulties; needs thousand pounds to clear himself; Bulstrode advised instead of involving himself in further obligations, Lydgate should become bankrupt
- **Lydgate's Awareness of Bulstrode's Nature**: Reflects on Bulstrode's contradictory character: unsympathetic fellow about some people, yet has taken great trouble and spent money on benevolent objects; Bulstrode seems to have some test by which he finds out whom Heaven cares for—has made up his mind it doesn't care for Lydgate
- **Current Domestic Crisis**: Upon returning home from visiting Raffles at Stone Court, found Dover's agent had already put a man in the house; found Rosamond stretched on bed pale and silent, without answer in her face to any word or look of his; sat down by bed and spoke with almost a cry of prayer
- **Treatment Philosophy**: Strongly convinced against prevalent practice of allowing alcohol and persistently administering large doses of opium in alcoholic poisoning cases; had repeatedly acted on conviction with favorable result; formed this conviction while abroad, stirred by publication of Dr. Ware's abundant experience in America

**Rosamond Lydgate (née Vincy)**
- Married to Lydgate; victorious obstinacy never wasting energy
- **Manipulation and Consequences**: Manipulated husband to go riding; accident at Halsell Wood led to loss of baby; regaining brilliant health
- Now possesses knowledge of Casaubon's codicil mentioning Will
- **Response to Debt Crisis**: When Lydgate proposed debt must be paid, fell like mortal chill; when presented with house-selling proposal, went to Mrs. Plymdale with congratulations instead; had secretly disobeyed by asking father for help; father said more likely to want help himself
- **Business Intervention**: Called on Mr. Borthrop Trumbull at his office; revoked Lydgate's order before New Year's Day party
- **Written to Sir Godwin with Refusal**: Had written requesting aid; awaited answer for nearly three weeks; Sir Godwin refused all aid; stated wife should not write on business; cannot supply thousand pounds or half that sum
- **Current Response to Crisis**: Told Lydgate her papa and mamma wish her to go and stay with them while things in miserable state; papa said he could do nothing about debt—if he paid this, there would be half-a-dozen more; she had better come back home again till Lydgate had got comfortable home for her; asked Lydgate: "Do you object, Tertius?"
- **Dynamics with Lydgate**: His tenderness towards her, both emotional prompting and well-considered resolve, inevitably interrupted by outbursts of indignation either ironical or remonstrant; she thought them totally unwarranted; repulsion his exceptional severity excited in her in danger of making more persistent tenderness unacceptable

**Mr. Bulstrode**
- **Raffles at Stone Court**: Raffles currently at Stone Court, showing mental and physical change from earlier terrifying behavior; instead of loud tormenting mood, shows intense vague terror and deprecates Bulstrode's anger; believes money all gone—has been robbed, half taken from him; came here because ill and somebody hunting him; told nobody anything, kept mouth shut
- **Raffles's Confused State**: Links of consciousness interrupted in Raffles; his minute terror-stricken narrative to Caleb Garth was delivered under set of visionary impulses which had dropped back into darkness; when Bulstrode taxed him with falsehood in saying he hadn't told anything (since he told man who took him up in gig), Raffles denied with solemn adjurations
- **Bulstrode's Uncertainty**: Heart sank at sign he could get no grasp over Raffles's wretched mind; could not trust any word of Raffles as to fact he most wanted to know: whether or not Raffles had really kept silence except to Caleb Garth; housekeeper reported without constraint that since Garth left, Raffles asked for beer and after that had not spoken, seeming very ill; might be concluded there had been no betrayal; Mrs. Abel thought strange man belonged to unpleasant "kin" among troubles of rich
- **Summoning Lydgate to Stone Court**: Called Lydgate in to attend to Raffles, describing him as unfortunate man once in his employment many years ago who went to America and returned to idle dissolute life; destitute, has claim on Bulstrode; slightly connected with Rigg, former owner of place; apparently mind affected; Bulstrode feels bound to do utmost for him
- **Lydgate's Assessment**: When asked Raffles's name, Lydgate was not disposed to say unnecessary word to Bulstrode, remembering last conversation; responded with bowed acknowledgment before entering room; examined Raffles and advised man had robust constitution, should not expect attack to be fatal though system in ticklish state; should be well watched and attended to; advised no liquors of any sort; believed men in his condition oftener killed by treatment than disease; stated he may pass to worse stage but shouldn't wonder if got better in few days by adhering to prescribed treatment; said new symptoms may arise and promised to come again tomorrow morning
- **Bulstrode's Earlier Actions**: Approximately fifteen months after Peter Featherstone's death, became proprietor of Stone Court through Joshua Rigg's land sale
- **Past Life**: Young banker's clerk; eminent though young member of Calvinistic dissenting church; became confidential accountant in Dunkirk's pawnbroker's business; magnificent profit from easy reception of goods without strict inquiry; perpetual self-justification; soul saturated with belief he did everything for God's sake; yet if could go back in youthful poverty would choose to be missionary
- **Later Years**: Wife died after five years; gradually withdrew capital but did not make sacrifices to end business, carried on for thirteen years before collapsing; became banker, Churchman, public benefactor
- **Offer to Will and Reaction**: Wrote letter to Will; met with Will at Shrubs; Will asked if Bulstrode connected with pawnbroker's business; Bulstrode felt suddenly uncertain; could not tell lie; answered falteringly that Will conjectured rightly; offered five hundred pounds yearly during his life and proportional capital at death; when Will rejected money and departed with determined quickness, Bulstrode suffered violent reaction and wept like woman
- **Plans for Change**: Change of plan determined by severe experience since Raffles recognized Will Ladislaw; banker had vainly attempted act of restitution which might move Divine Providence to arrest painful consequences; contemplates temporary withdrawal from management of much business; thinking of changing residence for a time; probably will close or let 'The Shrubs' and take place near coast under advice as to salubrity

**Mr. Raffles**
- Known to Bulstrode from twenty-five years prior; addresses him as "Nick"; claims to be visiting stepson Joshua Rigg
- Recalled name was "Ladislaw" and wrote it down in pocket-book; deliberately decided NOT to tell Bulstrode—holds secret knowledge of connection between Bulstrode and Ladislaw, intentionally concealing, treating as card to play
- Currently at Stone Court, seriously ill with affected mind; in painful dream and violent state; picked up by Caleb Garth in his gig after getting down from coach, walking beyond turning from toll-house; recognized Caleb from previous meeting; Caleb provided shelter
- Has revealed to Caleb Garth information about Bulstrode's harmful past life: that Bulstrode led harmful life for gain, kept others out of their rights by deceit
- **Current State at Stone Court**: Shows intense vague terror instead of earlier loud tormenting mood; deprecates Bulstrode's anger; claims money all gone, has been robbed, half taken from him; says came because ill and somebody hunting him; told nobody anything, kept mouth shut; consciousness interrupted; minute narrative to Caleb delivered under visionary impulses now dropped into darkness

**Mr. Farebrother (Vicar)**
- Aware Lydgate is proud man; had been playing whist to satisfy mother
- **Intervention with Fred and Mary**: Left whist-table to speak with Lydgate, disclosing Lydgate had done him service by influencing him to stop playing for money; later approached Fred at billiard-table; confessed temptation to let Fred ruin himself; disclosed satisfaction of Fred's affections stands in way of his own; warned Mary's affection is "conditionally bound"; claimed another man might win firm place through companionship of ready sympathy; overcame temptation to act selfishly
- Watching Mary Garth with evident admiration while she tells Rumpelstiltskin tale
